s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: to cause an object to extend in space (for example, by becoming straight, unfolded, or uncoiled){N:001}
s.g: to stretch out; to extend; to reach out

s.dp: Linear Movement › Fall
s.d: to fall from a particular point or location
s.g: to fall; to fall from; to fall off

s.dp: Maritime Activities
s.d: (a technical, nautical term) to drift off or be blown off one’s course and hence run aground
s.g: to run aground; to be blown off course and run aground

s.dp: Association › Join, Begin To Associate
s.d: to abandon a former relationship or association, or to dissociate (a type of reversal of beginning to associate){N:001}
s.g: to fall away; to forsake; to turn away
s.c: Note, however, that the underlying structure of the expression τῆς χάριτος ἐξεπέσατε really involves ‘turning away from God who has shown grace.’ For another interpretation of ἐκπίπτω in ⟦Galatians 5:4|Galatians 5:4⟧, see LN 90.72.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to change for the worse, with emphasis upon extent and suddenness

s.dp: Adequate, Qualified
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐκπίπτω<SDBG:ἐκπίπτω:000000>}[a] ‘to fall out or from,’ {D:15.120}) to become inadequate for some function

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to no longer experience a state or condition
s.g: to be outside of; to experience no longer
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐκπίπτω in ⟦Galatians 5:4|Galatians 5:4⟧, see LN 34.26.

s.dp: Maritime Activities
s.d: to sail out of an area
s.g: to sail out of port; to sail away from

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to cause to happen, with the implication of fulfilling some purpose{N:001}
s.g: to cause to happen; to make happen; to fulfill

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
s.d: the totality of a period of time, with the implication of proper completion{N:001}

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Surprise, Astonish
s.d: to be so amazed as to be practically overwhelmed

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐκπνέω ‘to breathe out,’ not occurring in the NT) to engage in the final act of dying
s.g: to die; to breathe out one’s last

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move out of an enclosed or well-defined two or three-dimensional area
s.g: to go out of; to depart out of; to leave from within
s.c: In some contexts one may interpret occurrences of ἐκπορεύομαι as being used figuratively or as part of an idiomatic phrase, but ἐκπορεύομαι also implies some type of movement out from a defined or enclosed area. Note, for example, the occurrences of ἐκπορεύομαι in the following contexts: τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ‘that which comes from a man’s mouth causes him to be defiled’ ⟦Matthew 15:11|Matthew 15:11⟧; ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς πάντα τόπον τῆς περιχώρου ‘the report about him went out into all parts of the surrounding region’ ⟦Luke 4:37|Luke 4:37⟧; τά τε πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκπορεύεσθαι ‘the evil spirits would go out of them’ ⟦Acts 19:12|Acts 19:12⟧. In a number of languages, however, it may be necessary to translate the meaning of ἐκπορεύομαι in quite different ways. For example, in ⟦Matthew 15:11|Matthew 15:11⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘that which a man says causes him to be defiled,’ and in ⟦Luke 4:37|Luke 4:37⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘more and more people in all parts of the surrounding region heard about Jesus,’ and for ⟦Acts 19:12|Acts 19:12⟧ it may be necessary to say ‘the evil spirits would no longer ride them’ or ‘… control them.’

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: (idiom, literally: to go in and to go out) to live or to conduct oneself in relationship to some community or group
s.g: to live with; to live among
s.c: The semantic focus of these idioms, especially in ⟦Acts 1:21|Acts 1:21⟧ and ⟦Acts 9:28|Acts 9:28⟧, appears to be the manner in which a person conducts himself in relationship to others, but it is possible to imply a certain amount of movement. For example, in ⟦Acts 1:21|Acts 1:21⟧ it is possible to translate ‘during the whole time the Lord Jesus travelled about with us,’ and in ⟦Acts 9:28|Acts 9:28⟧ one could translate ‘Paul stayed with them and went about in Jerusalem.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sexual Misbehavior
s.d: to engage in sexual immorality of any kind, often with the implication of prostitution
s.g: to engage in illicit sex; to commit fornication; sexual immorality; fornication; prostitution

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐκπτύω ‘to spit out,’ not occurring in the NT) to reject, with the implication of a measure of disdain
s.g: to reject; to have disdain for
s.c: In a number of languages ‘to reject’ is expressed idiomatically as ‘to throw away,’ ‘to push away,’ or ‘to turn one’s back toward.’

s.dp: Agriculture
s.d: to remove a plant, including its roots
s.g: to uproot; to pull out by the roots

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Surprise, Astonish
s.d: a state of intense amazement, to the point of being beside oneself with astonishment
s.c: In many languages it is simply impossible to speak of ‘being beside oneself with astonishment’ or ‘having astonishment seize someone.’ Though such expressions may seem quite appropriate in English, literal renderings of such statements may be almost totally meaningless in other languages. In ⟦Mark 5:42|Mark 5:42⟧, for example, one may readily translate ‘they were extremely astonished’ or in ⟦Luke 5:26|Luke 5:26⟧, ‘they were all very much astonished.’|In a number of languages, of course, astonishment is expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘they had to look three times’ or ‘they looked but they couldn’t believe.’

s.dp: Communication › Non-Verbal Communication
s.d: a vision accompanied by an ecstatic psychological state

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: to have departed from the patterns of correct behavior and thus to have become corrupt
s.g: to be corrupt; to have become corrupt

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Riot
s.d: to cause people to riot against
s.g: to stir up against; to start a riot; to cause an uproar

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: to cause an object to extend in space (for example, by becoming straight, unfolded, or uncoiled){N:001}
s.g: to stretch out; to extend; to reach out

s.dp: Control, Rule › Seize, Take into Custody
s.d: (an idiom, literally to stretch out hands upon) to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity

s.dp: Aspect › Complete, Finish, Succeed
s.d: to bring an activity to a successful finish{N:001}
s.g: to complete; to finish; to end; to accomplish

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
s.d: a state of eagerness involving perseverance over a period of time

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐκτείνω<SDBG:ἐκτείνω:000000>} ‘to stretch out,’ {D:16.19}) pertaining to an unceasing activity, normally involving a degree of intensity and/or perseverance
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐκτενής in ⟦1 Peter 4:8|1 Peter 4:8⟧, see ἐκτενής LN 25.71.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
s.d: pertaining to being eager to persevere in some state or activity
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐκτενής in ⟦1 Peter 4:8|1 Peter 4:8⟧, see ἐκτενής LN 68.12.

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐκτείνω<SDBG:ἐκτείνω:000000>} ‘to stretch out,’ {D:16.19}) pertaining to an unceasing activity, normally involving a degree of intensity and/or perseverance
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐκτενῶς in ⟦Acts 12:5|Acts 12:5⟧, see LN 25.71.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
s.d: pertaining to being eager to persevere in some state or activity
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐκτενῶς in ⟦Acts 12:5|Acts 12:5⟧, see ἐκτενῶς LN 68.12.

s.dp: Existence in Space › Put, Place
s.d: to put or place something out of an area

s.dp: Communication › Interpret, Mean, Explain
s.d: to explain something, presumably by putting forward additional or different information

s.dp: Non-Linear Movement
s.d: to shake something out or off, in order to get rid of an object or a substance
s.g: to shake off; to shake out; to shake from
s.c: In a number of languages quite different terms for shaking will be required for the contexts of ⟦Acts 28:5|Acts 28:5⟧ and ⟦Luke 9:5|Luke 9:5⟧, since in the first instance it is an animate being which clings, and in the second instance it is simply a substance that adheres.|In a number of languages, however, the symbolic meaning of ‘shaking dust off one’s feet’ is not at all clear, so that it may be necessary to add a type of classifier to indicate that such an action symbolizes the breaking off of association. It is for this reason that the expression ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια in ⟦Acts 18:6|Acts 18:6⟧ is often translated as ‘he protested by shaking the dust from his clothes.’

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Around, About, Outside
s.d: a position not contained within a particular area

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Around, About, Outside
s.d: the outside surface of an object
s.c: The manner in which ἔξωθεν, ἐκτός, and ὄπισθεν may be rendered in particular contexts depends very largely upon what is being spoken about. For example, ἔξωθεν in ⟦1 Peter 3:3|1 Peter 3:3⟧ refers to the outward aids employed in making oneself beautiful, but instead of speaking of such objects as being on the surface or on the outside, it may be necessary to speak of those things which one puts on the body or what one wears.

s.dp: Relations › Contrast
s.d: a marker of a contrast involving an exception

s.dp: Relations › Dissociation
s.d: a marker of dissociation in the sense of being independent from someone or something
s.g: from; free from; apart from; independent of

s.dp: Number › First, Second, Third, Etc. [Ordinals]
s.d: sixth in a series involving either time, space, or set

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: to wrench or sprain the ligaments of a joint, especially in the legs and feet
s.c: It is often possible to speak of ‘being wrenched’ as ‘being twisted.’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐκτρέπομαι ‘to turn from,’ not occurring in the NT) to turn away from the truth and to believe something which is different
s.g: to go astray; to stray after; to turn from and to follow

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to avoid becoming involved in some type of activity
s.g: to avoid; to not become involved

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to provide food for, with the implication of a considerable period of time and the food being adequate nourishment{N:001}
s.g: to provide food for; to give food to someone to eat

s.dp: Help, Care For › Rear, Bring Up
s.d: to raise a child to maturity by providing for physical and psychological needs{N:002}
s.g: to raise; to rear; to bring up
s.c: To raise or bring up children may be expressed in a number of different ways, for example, ‘to give food to children,’ ‘to take care of children,’ ‘to be a parent to children,’ ‘to cause a child to become an adult,’ or ‘to make a child become like oneself.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Birth, Procreation
s.d: an untimely or premature birth
s.c: There is a certain fundamental problem involved in the rendering of ἔκτρωμα in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:8|1 Corinthians 15:8⟧. Here Paul refers to himself, but the event in question is the appearance of Jesus to Paul, evidently on the road to Damascus. The reference, therefore, would seem to be his being born as a Christian. This spiritual birth, however, would appear to be rather late in the process rather than premature. It is for this reason that it may be wise to translate ἔκτρωμα in some instances as ‘untimely birth’ or ‘born at the wrong time,’ rather than indicating that he was ‘born too soon.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Carry, Bear
s.d: to carry something out of a structure or area
s.g: to carry out; to take out; to bring out

s.dp: Linear Movement › Lead, Bring, Take
s.d: to lead or bring out of a structure or area
s.g: to lead out; to bring forth

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to cause the growth and production of plants

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to flee from or out of
s.g: to flee out of; to flee from; to escape

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Become Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to become safe from danger by avoiding or escaping{N:001}
s.c: The meaning of this part of ⟦Romans 2:3|Romans 2:3⟧ is ‘to become free from the danger of being judged by God.’ ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι ‘in order that you may be able to escape all of these things that are going to happen’ ⟦Luke 21:36|Luke 21:36⟧. In ⟦Romans 2:3|Romans 2:3⟧ and ⟦Luke 21:36|Luke 21:36⟧ ἐκφεύγω should not be understood in the literal sense of running away from (see LN 15.63). The meaning is simply not to become involved in such danger.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Fear, Terror, Alarm
s.d: to cause someone to become terrified or very much afraid

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Fear, Terror, Alarm
s.d: pertaining to being extremely afraid{N:001}
s.g: very frightened; terrified; very much afraid

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to begin vegetative growth, with special emphasis upon the sprouting of leaves
s.c: The initial stages of growth, either of a plant as a whole or in the renewal of foliage after a winter or dry season, may be expressed in a number of ways, for example, ‘to become green again,’ ‘to show leaves,’ ‘to see leaves begin,’ or ‘when leaves unfold.’

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Movement of Liquids or Masses
s.d: to cause to pour out

s.dp: Linear Movement › Disperse, Scatter
s.d: to scatter a substance or mass

s.dp: Quantity › Abundance, Excess, Sparing
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐκχέω<SDBG:ἐκχέω:000000>}[a] ‘to pour out,’ {D:47.4}) to cause to exist in an abundance
s.g: to give in abundance; to bestow generously

s.dp: Case › To Cause To Experience
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐκχέω<SDBG:ἐκχέω:000000>}[a] ‘to pour out,’ {D:47.4}) to cause someone to experience something in an abundant or full manner

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: to flow out of a container{N:002}
s.g: to flow out; to pour out

s.dp: Aspect › Do Intensely or Extensively
s.d: to give oneself over completely to some activity or state
s.g: to give oneself over to; to plunge into; to commit oneself totally to

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐκχέω<SDBG:ἐκχέω:000004>}[e] ‘to flow out,’ {D:14.18}) to be involved in experiencing something in an abundant manner
s.g: to fully experience; to become fully involved

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐκχέομαι ‘to pour out oneself,’ not occurring in the NT) to give oneself completely to some type of behavior
s.g: to give oneself to; to devote oneself to

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to pour out blood) to cause the death of someone by violent means
s.c: The phrase πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον in ⟦Matthew 23:35|Matthew 23:35⟧ may be literally translated as ‘all innocent blood that is poured out.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (an idiom, literally: the blood pours out) to die, with the implication of a sacrificial purpose
s.g: to die as a sacrifice; sacrificial death
s.c: The relations between the various elements in this clause in ⟦Matthew 26:28|Matthew 26:28⟧ must in some instances be made somewhat more specific, for example, ‘by my dying, I am like a sacrifice for many for the purpose of their sins being forgiven.’ See also LN 23.107.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move out of or away from a place, with a possible implication of a considerable distance separating a person from the earlier location
s.g: to depart; to leave; to go out of

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: the process of dying
s.c: In a number of languages clear distinctions are made in the use of terms for dying on the basis of the manner or circumstances of death. For example, one term may refer to death primarily as the result of old age, while another term may refer to death caused by sickness, and still other terms may be used for death caused by violence. Careful distinctions must be used in determining the choice of terms based on particular contexts.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Willing
s.d: pertaining to being willing to do something without being forced or pressured
s.g: willing; willingly; of one’s own free will
s.c: In a number of languages ‘willingness’ to perform some action is expressed negatively, for example, ‘not having to’ or ‘not being forced to’ or ‘not being told one must.’ A positive expression of ‘willingness’ may be indicated idiomatically by a phrase such as ‘my heart approves.’

s.dp: Plants › Trees
s.d: tree reaching up to 10 m. high, but usually pruned to around 5 m.; leaves are grayish green above, and whitish underneath; fruit of the olive is about 2 cm. long and a bit more than a cm thick with a hard stone inside and a soft skin that covers the oily flesh; fruit is used for food and oil for cooking, for lamps, for rubbing on the body, for medicine, and in religion (anointing)
s.c: As in the case of other terms for trees which may not be identified by specific receptor-language terms, one can employ a generic expression followed by a borrowed term, for example, ‘a tree producing fruit called olives.’ In the context of ⟦Matthew 21:1|Matthew 21:1⟧ and similar passages it is important that ‘Mount of Olives’ not be rendered in such a way as to suggest that it was a mountain consisting of olives or even a mountain consisting of olive trees. A more appropriate expression in some languages is ‘a mountain known for its olive trees’ or ‘a mountain on which many olive trees grow.’ In a number of languages, however, it is important to employ a term such as ‘hill’ rather than ‘mountain,’ since the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem would be regarded in most receptor languages as a ‘hill’ not a ‘mountain.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a ridge to the east of Jerusalem, with the Kidron Valley in between

s.dp: Plants › Fruit Parts of Plants
s.d: fruit of the olive tree; about 2 cm. long and a bit more than a cm thick with a hard stone inside and a soft skin that covers the oily flesh; used for food and oil for cooking, for lamps, for rubbing on the body, for medicine, and in religion (anointing)
s.c: Since in some languages a term for ‘olive oil’ (ἔλαιον, LN 6.202) is better known than the fruit itself, one may employ a descriptive phrase such as ‘the fruit of olive oil’ or ‘the fruit that produces olive oil.’ In certain instances olives are actually known as ‘the cooking-oil fruit.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Plant Products
s.d: oil extracted from the fruit of olive trees, used as food, medicine, for burning in lamps, and as perfume when mixed with sweet-smelling substances{N:001}
s.c: See discussion of translational problems in LN 6.197.

s.dp: Plants › Trees
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐλαία<SDBG:ἐλαία:000000>}[a] ‘olive tree,’ {D:3.9}) a number of olive trees planted in a garden or grove
s.c: In ⟦Acts 1:12|Acts 1:12⟧, it may be well to employ the more common designation for ‘the hill called The Olive Grove,’ namely, ‘Hill of Olives’ or ‘Mount of Olives’ (see LN 3.9).

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (alternative form of Ἐλυμαῖος, derivative of Ἐλυμαίς ‘Elumais’ or ‘Elam,’ not occurring in the NT) a person who is a native of Elam

s.dp: Quantity › Many, Few [Countables]
s.d: a relatively small quantity on any dimension

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: pertaining to being of less status than something else

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a living being who is relatively young, often the younger of two objects

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Need, Lack
s.d: to possess too little of some substance
s.g: to have too little; to have less

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: to cause something to have less status or rank

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: to decrease in status or rank
s.c: Compare αὐξάνω ‘to become more important’ LN 87.37.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Drive Along, Carry Along
s.d: to cause an object to move by means of a strong force or vigorous action
s.g: to drive along; to carry along
s.c: In ⟦Luke 8:29|Luke 8:29⟧ ἐλαύνω occurs in the statement ἠλαύνετο ὑπὸ τοῦ δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους ‘he was driven into the desert by the demon.’ In this context it would appear that the demon was regarded as a type of force, parallel perhaps to wind.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: behavior characterized by caprice and instability
s.c: In some instances ἐλαφρία may be rendered in ⟦2 Corinthians 1:17|2 Corinthians 1:17⟧ as ‘not thinking about what I was doing’ or ‘not keeping the same thoughts about what I was doing.’

s.dp: Weight › Heavy, Light
s.d: pertaining to being relatively light in weight
s.c: Though in ⟦Matthew 11:30|Matthew 11:30⟧ ἐλαφρός can be understood in a literal sense, the entire statement in this verse is, of course, figurative. Therefore, one can also interpret ἐλαφρός in ⟦Matthew 11:30|Matthew 11:30⟧ as figurative (see LN 22.38). Note, however, that the phrase ὁ … ζυγός μου does not refer to something which Christ carries but to something which he places upon his followers. The same is true of the phrase τὸ φορτίον μου ‘my burden,’ which is the burden he gives to his disciples or servants.

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: a strictly limited point on the lower part of a scale of extent

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Easy, Light
s.d: pertaining to that which is easy to bear or endure
s.c: It is possible to render ἐλαφρός in ⟦Matthew 11:30|Matthew 11:30⟧ as ‘light,’ in the sense of ‘light in weight’ (see LN 86.2). However, if ‘burden’ in ⟦Matthew 11:30|Matthew 11:30⟧ is understood figuratively, ἐλαφρός can generally also be understood in a figurative sense.

s.dp: Features of Objects › Large, Small
s.d: a small size, relative to the norm for the class of objects in question
s.c: Note that in the case of a Greek superlative such as ἐλάχιστος, the meaning is not ‘the smallest’ but simply ‘very small.’ This is typical of many uses of the superlative in Greek.

s.dp: Value › Important, Unimportant
s.d: pertaining to being of the least importance
s.g: of least importance; of very little importance

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: pertaining to being of the lowest status

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mercy, Merciless
s.d: to show kindness or concern for someone in serious need
s.g: to show mercy; to be merciful toward; to have mercy on; mercy

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mercy, Merciless
s.d: to show kindness or concern for someone in serious need
s.g: to show mercy; to be merciful toward; to have mercy on; mercy

s.dp: Communication › Rebuke
s.d: to state that someone has done wrong, with the implication that there is adequate proof of such wrongdoing
s.g: to rebuke; to reproach; rebuke; reproach

s.dp: True, False
s.d: the evidence, normally based on argument or discussion, as to the truth or reality of something

s.dp: Communication › Rebuke
s.d: to state that someone has done wrong, with the implication that there is adequate proof of such wrongdoing
s.g: to rebuke; to reproach; rebuke; reproach

s.dp: Communication › Rebuke
s.d: to state that someone has done wrong, with the implication that there is adequate proof of such wrongdoing
s.g: to rebuke; to reproach; rebuke; reproach

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mercy, Merciless
s.d: pertaining to being deserving of pity in view of one’s miserable condition

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: to give to those in need as an act of mercy
s.g: acts of charity; alms; giving to the needy

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: (semantic derivative of {L:ἐλεημοσύνη<SDBG:ἐλεημοσύνη:000000>}[a] ‘giving to the needy,’ {D:57.111}) that which is given to help the needy
s.g: gift; money given to the needy; charity donation
s.c: In some languages the closest equivalent of ἐλεημοσύνη in ⟦Acts 3:2|Acts 3:2⟧ is simply ‘money.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mercy, Merciless
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐλεάω<SDBG:ἐλεάω:000000>} ‘to show mercy,’ {D:88.76}) pertaining to showing mercy

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mercy, Merciless
s.d: to show kindness or concern for someone in serious need
s.g: to show mercy; to be merciful toward; to have mercy on; mercy

s.dp: Control, Rule › Release, Set Free
s.d: the state of being free
s.c: In a number of languages the concept of freedom is expressed as a negation of control or domination, for example, ‘where the Spirit of the Lord is present, there is no longer domination’ or ‘… a person is not dominated’ or ‘… a person does not feel under constraint.’

s.dp: Control, Rule › Release, Set Free
s.d: pertaining to being free

s.dp: Status › Slave, Free
s.d: pertaining to a person who is not a slave, either one who has never been a slave or one who was a slave formerly but is no longer

s.dp: Control, Rule › Release, Set Free
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐλεύθερος<SDBG:ἐλεύθερος:000000>}[a] ‘free,’ {D:37.134}) to cause someone to be set free or to be released

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move toward or up to the reference point of the viewpoint character or event{N:001}

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: (derivative of ἐλέφας ‘elephant,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to consisting of the tusks of elephants
s.g: consisting of ivory; made of ivory
s.c: Since ivory, whether of elephant or walrus tusks, is well known throughout the world, there are usually few problems involved in finding a satisfactory term. However, where a term for ‘ivory’ is not known, one can always speak of ‘beautiful bone.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the son of Abiud in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the son of Melea in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus ({S:04000101400030})

s.g: to roll up; to make into a roll

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: a painful, ulcerated sore resulting from infection

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἕλκος<SDBG:ἕλκος:000000>} ‘sore, ulcer,’ {D:23.179}) to have sores on the body
s.g: to have sores; to have ulcers; to be full of sores

s.dp: Linear Movement › Pull, Draw, Drag
s.d: to pull or drag, requiring force because of the inertia of the object being dragged
s.g: to pull; to drag; to draw

s.dp: Linear Movement › Lead, Bring, Take
s.d: to drag or pull by physical force, often implying resistance
s.g: to drag; to lead by force

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: Greece

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Ethnic-Cultural
s.d: a person who participates in Greek culture and in so doing would speak the Greek language, but not necessarily a person of Greek ethnic background
s.c: In ⟦Romans 1:14|Romans 1:14⟧ it is possible that the contrast Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις may be interpreted as ‘to the Greek-speaking persons and to those who do not speak Greek,’ but the entire context of ⟦Romans 1:14|Romans 1:14⟧ points to a somewhat broader designation.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: (an extended meaning of {L:Ἕλλην<SDBG:Ἕλλην:000000>}[a] ‘Greek,’ {D:11.90}) a person who is a Gentile in view of being a Greek
s.c: Though the occurrence of Ἕλλην in ⟦John 7:35|John 7:35⟧ could be interpreted as merely a reference to Greeks, it is probably a reference to Greeks as being Gentiles, and therefore Ἕλλην is classified here in the subdomain of socio-religious groups. The occurrence of Ἕλλην in ⟦Acts 14:1|Acts 14:1⟧ (ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος ‘so that a large number of Jews and Gentiles believed’) is another instance of Ἕλλην referring primarily to a socio-religious group rather than merely to Greeks as a nation.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Ethnic-Cultural
s.d: pertaining to what is Greek
s.c: In rendering this expression in ⟦Revelation 9:11|Revelation 9:11⟧ it is often necessary to say ‘in the language spoken by the Greeks’ or ‘in the Greek language.’ Ελληνικός as an adjective does not denote the Greek language as such, but in the feminine form the reference would be to γλῶσσα ‘language.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Ethnic-Cultural
s.d: a woman of Greek culture and language
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦Mark 7:26|Mark 7:26⟧ Ἑλληνίς is to be understood in the sense of Gentile (see LN 11.41), for the account seems to focus upon the fact that this woman who was not a Jewess nevertheless displayed remarkable faith and confidence in Jesus’ ability to help.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: (an extended meaning of {L:Ἑλληνίς<SDBG:Ἑλληνίς:000000>}[a] ‘Greek woman,’ {D:11.91}) a female who is a Gentile in view of being a Greek
s.c: Though one may translate Ἑλληνίς in ⟦Acts 17:12|Acts 17:12⟧ as ‘Greek,’ the focus is probably upon these women as being Gentiles rather than merely Greeks, for it is the Gentile status of these persons which seems to have been particularly aggravating to some of the Jews in that region.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Ethnic-Cultural
s.d: a Greek-speaking Jew in contrast to one speaking a Semitic language
s.c: The Greek-speaking Jews were basically Jewish in culture and religion, but they had adopted certain customs typical of the larger Greco-Roman world in which many of them lived. This inevitably resulted in certain suspicions and misunderstandings.

s.dp: Communication › Language
s.g: in the Greek language; in Greek

s.dp: Communication › Written Language
s.d: to keep a record of something
s.c: There may be difficulties involved in changing the passive expression ‘no account is kept of sins’ in ⟦Romans 5:13|Romans 5:13⟧ to ‘God doesn’t keep an account of sins,’ for this might imply that God was unconcerned about sin. It is sometimes possible to avoid this difficulty by rendering ‘no account is kept of sins’ as ‘a sin is not listed as a sin.’

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Keep Records
s.d: to charge to an account

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Hope, Look Forward To
s.d: to look forward with confidence to that which is good and beneficial
s.g: to hope; to hope for; hope

s.dp: Think › To Think Concerning Future Contingencies
s.d: to expect, with the implication of some benefit{N:001}

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Hope, Look Forward To
s.d: to look forward with confidence to that which is good and beneficial
s.g: to hope; to hope for; hope

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Hope, Look Forward To
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐλπίζω<SDBG:ἐλπίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to hope,’ {D:25.59}) that which is hoped for

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Hope, Look Forward To
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐλπίζω<SDBG:ἐλπίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to hope,’ {D:25.59}) that which constitutes the cause or reason for hoping
s.g: the basis for hope; the reason for hope
s.c: This expression in ⟦1 Thessalonians 2:19|1 Thessalonians 2:19⟧ may be rendered in some languages as ‘for who is the one who causes us to hope and to have joy’ or ‘… to be happy.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a magician of Cyprus

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: a Hebrew term meaning my God
s.c: For certain problems involved in rendering an expression such as ‘my God,’ see the discussion in LN 12.1.

s.dp: Discourse Referentials › Speaker
s.d: a reflexive reference to the first person singular within the immediate context
s.c: For the plural, see LN 92.25.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go Into
s.d: to go into or onto, as in the case of a boat
s.g: to embark; to get into a boat
s.c: In certain contexts ἐμβαίνω occurs without a specific indication of a ship or boat in the immediate context, for example, πάλιν ἐμβὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν ‘again embarking, he left for the other side’ ⟦Mark 8:13|Mark 8:13⟧.|In a number of languages it is necessary to introduce into the context some specific reference to a boat or ship.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Walk, Step
s.d: to step into some area
s.g: to go into; to step into
s.c: This meaning is only found as a variant reading: ὁ οὖν πρῶτος ἐμβὰς μετὰ τὴν ταραχὴν τοῦ ὕδατος ὑγιὴς ἐγίνετο ‘the first one to go into (the pool) after the water was stirred up was healed’ ⟦John 5:3|John 5:3⟧ (apparatus).

s.dp: Existence in Space › Put, Place
s.d: to put or throw into a place
s.g: to put into; to throw into
s.c: Despite the use of the verb ἐμβάλλω in ⟦Luke 12:5|Luke 12:5⟧, the focus of meaning is not so much upon the act of throwing or hurling but rather upon the act of causing someone to be in a particular place.

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Use of Liquids
s.d: to dip an object in a liquid{N:001}

s.dp: Religious Activities › Religious Practice
s.d: The meaning of ἐμβατεύω, which occurs only once in the NT, namely, in {S:05100201800026}, is obscure. It may mean more or less literally ‘to set foot upon’ or ‘to enter’ or possibly ‘to come into possession of.’ It may also mean ‘to enter into’ in the sense of to go into detail in treating a subject, but it seems more likely that ἐμβατεύω in {S:05100201800026} is a technical term derived from the mystery religions, and it could be interpreted in the phrase ἅ ἑόρακεν ἐμβατεύων as meaning ‘who enters the sanctuary which he saw in ecstasy’ or ‘taking his stand on what he has seen in the mysteries.’ In view of the context, which speaks of someone being puffed up without cause, one might also render this Greek phrase as ‘by what he saw when he was initiated.’ For further data on this semantically difficult term, see A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, University of Chicago Press, third edition edited by Danker (BDAG).

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go Into
s.d: to cause someone to go into, as in the case of a boat
s.g: to cause to go aboard; to cause to embark
s.c: The causative in this type of context may be expressed simply as ‘he commanded us,’ or the causative may be somewhat weakened to a form such as in English ‘he had us go aboard.’

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to direct one’s vision and attention to a particular object
s.g: to look straight at; to look directly at
s.c: In ⟦John 1:36|John 1:36⟧ ἐμβλέπω may not differ significantly in meaning from βλέπω in ⟦John 1:29|John 1:29⟧ (see LN 24.7).

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to process information by giving consideration to various aspects{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages the concept of thinking is closely related to terms referring to perception. For example, in some languages one may speak of thinking as ‘to see with the heart’ or ‘to look at with the liver.’

s.dp: Communication › Insist
s.d: to state something with sternness

s.dp: Communication › Rebuke
s.d: to exhibit irritation or even anger in expressing a harsh reproof

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: to have an intense, strong feeling of concern, often with the implication of indignation
s.g: to feel strongly; to be indignant

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Processes Involving the Mouth, Other Than Eating and Drinking
s.c: Since a term meaning ‘to vomit’ often carries somewhat vulgar connotations, ἐμέω in ⟦Revelation 3:16|Revelation 3:16⟧ has frequently been translated as ‘to spit out of my mouth.’|It is also possible to interpret ‘to vomit out of the mouth’ as an idiom meaning ‘to reject.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Anger, Be Indignant With
s.d: to be so furiously angry with someone as to be almost out of one’s mind
s.g: to be enraged; to be infuriated; to be insanely angry
s.c: In some instances it may be possible to render ἐμμαίνομαι in ⟦Acts 26:11|Acts 26:11⟧ as ‘to be so angry as to be like an insane person.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a name attributed to Jesus Christ

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a village in Judea, not far from Jerusalem

s.dp: Existence in Space › Remain, Stay
s.d: to remain in the same place over a period of time{N:001}

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: to continue in an activity or state
s.g: to continue; to remain in; to keep on
s.c: In ⟦Hebrews 8:9|Hebrews 8:9⟧ the implication of ‘to continue in a covenant’ is to adhere to the articles or stipulations of a covenant. Accordingly, one may render ⟦Hebrews 8:9|Hebrews 8:9⟧ as ‘because they did not remain faithful to my covenant.’ In ⟦Acts 14:22|Acts 14:22⟧ (παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει ‘encourage them to remain true to the faith’), it is also possible to translate the expression ‘to remain true to the faith’ as ‘to continue to believe.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a man from whose sons Abraham bought a burial place

s.dp: Discourse Referentials › Speaker
s.d: pertaining to a speaker
